Because the Best Two Word Explanation for Marijuana Prohibition Is Still “Bad Journalism.”

It would be an understatement to say that journalism is in a crisis, but it has been a long time coming. A large segment of the American public has lost all confidence in what we now call “The Media.”

A little over 30 years ago, in 1994, Simon and Schuster published a book by Paul Weaver, News and the Culture of Lying, How Journalism Really Works, https://books.google.es/books/about/News_and_the_Culture_of_Lying.html?id=655ZAAAAMAAJ&redir_esc=y

It was widely praised, but not widely reviewed, for obvious reasons.

When I read it in 1995, I was the National Director of NORML.org, the National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws, and it certainly resonated with me.

For several years we had been trying, unsuccessfully, to get the elite mass media based in Washington just to report the number of Americans being arrested on marijuana changes, (588,963 in 1995, the most ever up until then).

Marijuana Arrests For 1995 Most Everhttps://norml.org/news/1996/10/17/marijuana-arrests-for-1995-most-ever/

But to no avail.

Nor would they report the fact that sick and dying Americans were using cannabis for medical purposes: We had people on crutches and in wheelchairs picketing the White House and at a very sparsely attended press conference at the National Press Club. We even put “Stop Arresting Sick People” on our letterheads. Nothing.

Nor would they report that the United States government was lying about The Netherlands, one of our oldest allies, where cannabis had been sold over the counter for 20 years, now almost 50.

Drug Czars even went to Amsterdam and lied from there, to lend authenticity to their mendacity. Back in Washington, the Dutch embassy held a press conference to try to tell the truth, but no one came.

Paul Weaver had briefly mentioned the Drug War as one example of the deceit, but even he could not see what was hidden so well.

Unfortunately, his timing was also bad for longer term relevance. That was the beginning of the Internet age and just two years later in late 1997, after I had left NORML, l could begin doing MarijuanaNews.com with a new MicroSoft program called FrontPage97. Nature abhors a vacuum so badly it would even fill one with me.

For the first time in the history of journalism, it became possible to document the lying contemporaneously, which I have been doing — off and on — ever since. Not that it has had much of an impact, and the lying has never stopped, or even changed, up to the present.

The point in bringing back the archives is to demonstrate the persistence of the same memes. The more things change, the more the lying stays the same, and goes unreported.

I have joked that marijuana prohibition causes long term memory loss. If you don’t remember the past, you are doomed to repeat it, and you don’t know that you are still being lied to.

Now, almost thirty years later, twenty four states have more or less legalized recreational marijuana, and thirty nine have more or less legalized medical marijuana, the decades of “Prohibition” (a term that is still only used for alcohol during a period that ended over ninety years ago) has gone down the memory hole.

And the now over thirty million arrests (for simple possession), that we could not get the media even to mention, are also forgotten.

Even the fact that arrests continue at a rate of “only” two hundred thousand a year, and are still disproportionately non white, is still rarely reported.

Of course, it is being regularly reported that marijuana still legally classified as a Schedule 1 drug.

List of Schedule I controlled substances (U.S)

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Schedule_I_controlled_substances_(U.S.).

Meaning that it has no medical use and is as dangerous as heroin, but more dangerous than Schedule 2 drugs, such as cocaine, methamphetamine, methadone, hydromorphone (Dilaudid), meperidine (Demerol), oxycodone (OxyContin), fentanyl, Dexedrine, Adderall, and Ritalin.

But it is never reported why and how it was put there. It wasn’t done by the National Institutes of Health. but by John Mitchell, Nixon’s Attorney General, who went to prison for his role in the Watergate scandal. It should never have been in Schedule 1, in the first place.

And then there’s the breaking news that “marijuana today is much stronger than it used to be back when we all thought it was harmless.” The first time I heard that was back in the 1970s.

Of course, we got high way back then. And potency is only a problem when it’s contraband, and you don’t know what it is. Nonetheless, several leading publications have recently carried articles about this “new” threat. I will be publishing more about that very soon.

For context, you might want to start with the Frequently Asked Questions section. That section was all written in 1998. I hope my writing has improved. Their lying hasn’t.
